propositions: Three structurally similar O_EXCL lock acquisition loops exist across enrich_drain, compact_trigger, and gc_trigger, differing in release semantics, stamp bytes, and logging; consolidation is blocked by copy drift.

The drain's release uses one try block (os.close + unlink together), risking lock leakage on close failure; compact_trigger and gc_trigger use two independent try blocks, so consolidation must adopt the safer two-block form.
The drain writes newline-terminated stamps while the other workers do not; readers strip() both forms identically, so consolidation should adopt no-newline for consistency.

The drain's reclaim warning names the lock holder via _describe_drain_lock_holder and is contractually pinned to doctor_locks' phrasing by test_drain_and_doctor_describe_a_holderless_lock_identically; this naming must survive consolidation.

The six lock functions (_acquire_advisory_lock, _release_advisory_lock, _acquire_trigger_lock, release_trigger_lock, _acquire_worker_lock, release_worker_lock) are monkeypatched by name in test_lock_holder_labelling.py:134-135 and must remain module-level attributes.

After StorePaths landing, all three workers derive lock paths consistently through StorePaths or _gc_dir helpers, and directory creation mechanisms differ (drain/compaction use os.makedirs; gc uses Path.mkdir), so creation stays with callers while the shared helper takes a resolved path.
